newsitem.title: GERMANY: Widow of British builder wins German legal battle.
newsitem.headline: Widow of British builder wins German legal battle.

text.p: The widow of a British builder who fell to his death on a Leipzig building site in 1994 won a court victory on Wednesday when his former employers were found guilty of negligent manslaughter.
A regional east German court found David Carter and Richard Unterhuber, representing the British and German firms in charge of the building site, both guilty of negligent manslaughter.

Carter, who was also found in breach of safety regulations, was sentenced to a suspended jail term of five months and ordered to pay 8,000 marks compensation to Denise Stacey, who has led a three-year campaign to prosecute her husband's employers.
Unterhuber was ordered to pay a fine of 14,000 marks and received no jail sentence.
Len Stacey, 49, was killed when he fell head first from an eight-metre (26 Feet) raised section of a building site in the east German town.

Petra Wendtland, the judge who tried the case in the town of Eilenburg near Leipzig, said in a telephone interview after the verdict that Stacey's employers should have provided safety barriers on raised levels of the site.

According to German construction trade union IG Bau, nearly 600 workers a year die on German building sites, which often use illegal labour and have been accused of widespread failure to implement safety procedures.
Denise Stacey was not immediately available for comment after the verdict.
